outcomes.text: Define movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion and nutrition as characteristics of living organisms.
Compare plant, animal and bacterial cell structures; identify them in images; explain plant and animal cell functions; define cell organisation levels; and state specialised-cell functions.
Use magnification = image size ÷ actual size, calculate magnification or specimen size, and convert millimetres to micrometres.

topics.title: B3 Movement into and out of cells

outcomes.text: Describe diffusion, its cellular importance, and investigate how surface area, temperature, concentration gradient and distance affect its rate.
Describe osmosis and water movement through membranes; investigate concentration effects on plant tissues; explain turgor, plasmolysis and flaccidity.
Describe active transport against a concentration gradient using respiratory energy, and explain its importance including root-hair ion uptake.
Identify elements in carbohydrates, fats and proteins; describe their smaller-unit composition; and explain tests for starch, reducing sugars, proteins and fats.
Describe enzymes as protein biological catalysts; explain active sites, enzyme-substrate complexes, specificity and denaturation; and investigate temperature and pH effects.
Describe photosynthesis, state its word and balanced equations, explain chlorophyll’s role, and investigate requirements and effects of light, carbon dioxide, temperature and darkness.
Identify chloroplasts, cuticle, guard cells, stomata, epidermises, mesophyll, air spaces, vascular bundles, xylem and phloem in dicot leaves.
Define a balanced diet and state sources and importance of carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins C and D, calcium, iron, fibre and water.
Identify digestive organs and explain their roles in ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation and egestion.
Distinguish physical and chemical digestion, explain surface-area and absorption benefits, describe enzyme actions and locations, and state hydrochloric-acid functions.
State xylem and phloem functions, and identify their positions in root, stem and leaf sections of non-woody dicots.
Identify root hair cells, state their functions, explain their surface-area advantage, and outline water’s pathway through roots, xylem and mesophyll.
Define transpiration as leaf water-vapour loss and investigate how temperature and wind speed affect its rate.
Describe a circulatory system as vessels with a pump and valves that maintain one-way blood flow.
Identify heart structures; explain pumping, muscle contraction and valve action; describe monitoring methods; investigate activity effects; and explain coronary-heart-disease risks and prevention.
Describe artery, vein and capillary structures, and relate artery and vein structure to the pressure of transported blood.
List and identify blood components, state their functions in transport, defence and clotting, and explain how clotting prevents blood loss and pathogen entry.
Know pathogen and transmissible-disease definitions, transmission routes, body defences, virus features, disease control, and active immunity through infection or vaccination.
Identify breathing-system structures, investigate activity’s effects on breathing, and explain how human gas-exchange surfaces are adapted.
Understand energy uses, define aerobic respiration, and state its word and balanced symbol equations.
Define drugs, describe antibiotics against bacteria, distinguish bacterial and viral treatment, and explain limiting antibiotic resistance.
Identify flower structures and functions, explain pollination and fertilisation, and investigate conditions needed for seed germination.
Identify reproductive structures and functions, explain fertilisation, and describe menstrual-cycle changes in ovaries and uterine lining.
Recognise the Sun as the main energy source and describe energy transfer through organisms to the environment.
Construct and interpret food chains and webs, classify organisms by feeding roles, and assess human impacts on habitats.
Describe carbon movement through photosynthesis, respiration, feeding, decomposition, fossil-fuel formation, and combustion.
Define ecosystems and biodiversity, explain habitat destruction, and describe or explain deforestation’s environmental consequences.
Explain causes of endangerment or extinction and describe conservation through protection, education, captive breeding, and seed banks.
Compare states of matter, explain particle arrangements and movements, describe state changes, and relate gas volume to temperature and pressure.
Distinguish elements, compounds, and mixtures.

subtopics.title: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table

outcomes.text: Describe atomic structure, particle properties, atomic and mass numbers, electron configurations, and links between groups, periods, and electrons.
Explain ion formation, ionic bonding, ionic structures, and the characteristic properties of ionic compounds.
Explain covalent bonding in specified molecules and relate simple molecular structures to their physical and electrical properties.
Use chemical formulas, construct and balance equations, and deduce molecular or ionic formulas from models, atom ratios, or ion charges.
Define electrolysis, identify cell components, predict or identify electrode products, and describe observations for specified electrolytes.
Distinguish exothermic and endothermic reactions, interpret or draw energy pathways, define activation energy, and relate energy changes to bonds.
Identify physical and chemical changes and explain how they differ.
Explain and investigate reaction rates using collision theory, catalysts, experimental measurements, and data interpretation.
Define redox, oxidation, and reduction; identify oxygen gain or loss and determine oxidation and reduction in reactions.
Describe acid and base reactions, indicator effects, and compare neutrality, acidity and alkalinity using universal-indicator colours and pH.
Classify oxides as acidic or basic, relating their properties to whether the element is metallic or non-metallic.
Describe preparing, separating and purifying soluble salts using acids, and preparing insoluble salts by precipitation.
Describe the Periodic Table’s periods, groups and increasing proton number, metallic-to-non-metallic trend, and group trends.
Describe Group I metals and trends in melting point, density and water reactivity, and predict other Group I properties.
Describe Group VII halogen properties, appearances, trends and displacement reactions, and predict properties of other Group VII elements.
Describe transition elements as dense, high-melting metals that form coloured compounds and often act as catalysts.
Describe noble gases as unreactive monatomic gases and explain their low reactivity using electronic configuration.
Compare metals and non-metals by conductivity, malleability, ductility and melting or boiling points, including metal reactions.
Relate aluminium and copper uses to properties including low density, electrical conductivity, corrosion resistance and suitability for wiring.
Describe alloy composition, examples, uses and structural representations, and explain why alloys are harder and stronger than pure metals.
Recall the reactivity series, describe relevant metal reactions, explain them using series position, and deduce reactivity from results.
State the conditions for iron rusting and explain how painting, greasing and plastic coatings prevent oxygen and water contact.
Relate ore extraction difficulty to reactivity, describe iron extraction from hematite in a blast furnace, and state aluminium extraction from bauxite by electrolysis.
Test for water, explain why distilled water is preferred in chemistry, and describe domestic water treatment.
Know air composition, pollutant sources and effects, and strategies addressing climate change, acid rain and greenhouse-gas warming.
Define saturated and unsaturated compounds and homologous series, including their general formula and physical-property trends.
Identify fossil fuels and petroleum hydrocarbons, explain fractional distillation, name fraction uses, and describe trends up the column.
Describe alkanes as saturated hydrocarbons with single covalent bonds that are generally unreactive except during combustion.
Describe alkene structure, bromine testing, cracking manufacture, and addition reactions with bromine, hydrogen and steam.
Define polymers as molecules formed from monomers and identify poly(ethene) formation as addition polymerisation of ethene.

topics.title: C12 Experimental techniques and chemical analysis

outcomes.text: Select apparatus for measuring quantities and define solvent, solute, solution, saturated solution, residue and filtrate.
Use paper chromatography to separate soluble coloured mixtures, interpret chromatograms, and calculate Rf from travel distances.
Explain separation and purification using solvents, filtration, crystallisation, simple distillation or fractional distillation, and select suitable methods.
Describe chemical tests identifying specified anions, cations, gases and metal cations using flame tests.

topics.title: P1.1 Physical quantities and measurement techniques

subtopics.title: P1.1 Physical quantities and measurement techniques

outcomes.text: Measure lengths, volumes and time intervals, and obtain reliable averages for small distances and short times.
Define and calculate speed and acceleration, interpret motion graphs, and determine distance, speed and acceleration from graph features.
Explain effects of forces, determine resultant forces, describe friction and drag, apply Newton’s second law, and state inertia’s motion principle.
Distinguish mass, weight and gravitational field strength, and use their equations, including Earth’s approximate gravitational values.
Calculate density, determine densities experimentally for liquids and solids, and predict whether objects float or sink.
Describe energy stores and transfers, conservation, work, energy resources, efficiency, kinetic and potential energy, and power calculations.
Explain how pressure depends on force and area, and calculate pressure using force divided by area.

topics.title: P2.1 Kinetic particle model of matter

subtopics.title: P2.1 Kinetic particle model of matter

outcomes.text: Describe states of matter and particle behaviour, relate particle motion to temperature, and explain gas pressure and pressure changes.
Explain thermal expansion and evaporation, including particle escape, cooling, and factors affecting evaporation rate.
Describe conduction, convection and radiation, factors affecting thermal radiation, relevant experiments, and everyday applications and consequences.
Describe wave energy transfer, wave features, reflection, refraction, transverse and longitudinal waves, and calculate wave speed.
Explain that vibrating sources produce sound.
Recall the human audible frequency range as approximately 20 Hz to 20 kHz.
Know that sound requires a medium for transmission.
Determine sound speed in air by measuring distance and travel time.
Relate wave amplitude to loudness and frequency to pitch.
Describe an echo as reflected sound.
Define ultrasound as sound above 20 kHz.
Describe sound waves in air as longitudinal compressions and rarefactions.
Explain compressions as high-pressure regions where particles are closer together.
Explain rarefactions as low-pressure regions where particles are farther apart.
Know that sound generally travels fastest in solids, then liquids, then gases.
Explain sound production, audible frequencies, transmission through media, speed measurement, amplitude and frequency effects, echoes, ultrasound, and compressions and rarefactions.
Use ray diagrams to explain reflection, refraction, plane mirrors, converging lenses, image properties and dispersion.
Recall electromagnetic-spectrum order, speeds, applications and hazards, including effects of excessive ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma exposure.
State that electric charge can be positive or negative.
Describe attraction between unlike charges and repulsion between like charges.
Distinguish conductors from insulators and give typical examples.
State that charge is measured in coulombs.
Relate electric current to the flow of charge.
Define current as charge passing a point per unit time and use I = Q/t.
Relate current in metals to moving electrons.
Use analogue and digital ammeters with suitable ranges.
Distinguish direct current from alternating current.
Explain metallic conduction using delocalised electrons.
State conventional current flows positive to negative, while electrons flow oppositely.
Explain source voltage as causing current in a circuit.
Know that source voltage is shared among components in series.
Use analogue and digital voltmeters with suitable ranges.
Define e.m.f. as work done per unit charge around a complete circuit.
State that e.m.f. is measured in volts.
Define potential difference as work done per unit charge between two points.
State that potential difference is measured in volts.
Use the resistance equation R = V/I.
Know resistance increases directly with conductor length and decreases with cross-sectional area.
Explain how circuits transfer electrical energy from sources through components to surroundings.
Use the electrical power equation P = IV.
Use the electrical energy equation E = IVt.
Define kilowatt-hours and calculate appliance operating costs.
Draw and interpret circuits containing standard cells, switches, resistors, heaters, lamps, motors, meters and fuses.
Draw and interpret circuits containing generators and LEDs, including their behaviour.
Know that current is identical at every point in a series circuit.
Construct and use series and parallel circuits.
Calculate the combined resistance of resistors connected in series.
Explain the advantages of connecting lamps in parallel.
Know that source current in parallel exceeds the current in any individual branch.
Know that parallel combination resistance is less than either individual resistance.
Apply current and potential-difference rules at junctions and in series or parallel arrangements.
Calculate the combined resistance of two parallel resistors.
Describe the heating effect produced by electric current.
State hazards caused by damaged insulation, overheating cables, dampness and excessive current.
Explain fuses and trip switches, selecting suitable ratings and settings.
Explain why appliance casings must be insulating or earthed.
Know that cells and batteries convert chemical energy into electrical energy.
Know that generators convert kinetic energy into electrical energy.
Know that motors convert electrical energy into kinetic energy.
Understand charge, current, voltage, electromotive force, potential difference and resistance, including their measurement, equations, circuit behaviour and conduction in metals.
Draw and interpret diagrams containing cells, batteries, power supplies, switches, resistors, heaters, lamps, motors, ammeters, voltmeters and fuses, including their circuit behaviour.
Draw and interpret diagrams containing generators and LEDs, and explain how these components behave in circuits.
Recognise that current has the same value at every point in a series circuit.
Construct and use both series and parallel circuits.
Calculate the total resistance of two or more resistors connected in series.
Explain the benefits of connecting lamps in parallel.
Recognise that source current in a parallel circuit exceeds the current in any individual branch.
Know that two parallel resistors together have less resistance than either resistor alone.
Use junction-current and potential-difference rules for parallel and series circuits in calculations.
Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors connected in parallel.
Describe how an electric current produces heating.
Explain that cells and batteries convert chemical energy to electrical energy, generators convert kinetic energy to electrical energy, and motors convert electrical energy to kinetic energy.
Draw and interpret circuit diagrams containing cells, batteries, power supplies, switches, resistors, heaters, lamps, motors, ammeters, voltmeters and fuses, and describe their circuit behaviour.
Draw and interpret circuit diagrams containing generators and LEDs, and describe how these components behave in a circuit.
Know that current is the same at every point in a series circuit.
Calculate the combined resistance of two or more resistors connected in series.
Know that source current in a parallel circuit exceeds the current in any individual branch.
Know that two resistors in parallel have a combined resistance lower than either resistor alone.
Use calculations involving current at parallel junctions and potential differences in series and parallel circuits.
Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors connected in parallel.
Describe the Solar System as the Sun, eight ordered planets, minor planets, asteroids and planetary moons.
Know the Sun is Earth’s nearest star and that light-years measure astronomical distances.
Calculate light travel time across significant Solar System distances.
Explain that the Sun’s mass causes the planets to orbit it.
Define orbital speed using v = 2πr/T and apply the equation.
Explain that solar gravitational attraction keeps objects in orbit.
Describe the Sun as a medium-sized hydrogen-and-helium star radiating infrared, visible and ultraviolet energy.
Know solar gravitational strength and planetary orbital speeds decrease with increasing distance from the Sun.
Explain that stable stars release energy through hydrogen-to-helium nuclear fusion.
Explain that gravity forms stable protostars from interstellar gas and dust.
Describe how a star’s mass determines its subsequent life cycle.
Know that supernova remnants can form new stars with orbiting planets.
Describe galaxies as billions of stars, including the Sun in the Milky Way.
Know that other Milky Way stars are much farther from Earth than the Sun.
Know the Milky Way is one of billions of galaxies and is about 100,000 light-years across.
Describe Big Bang evidence and its model of an approximately 13.8-billion-year-old, expanding Universe originating from a hot, dense point.
Describe the Solar System as containing the Sun, eight ordered planets, minor planets including dwarf planets and asteroids, and moons orbiting planets.
Explain stellar structure, orbital motion, star life cycles, galaxies, the Milky Way, and evidence and principles of the expanding Universe.
